subject: Novamed: request for attestation on surgical deletion & per-tenant log retention
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novamed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: legal@novamed.com
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: per-tenant delete + CAIQ/SIG evidence request

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Our security team ran the CAIQ/SIG scan and has two focused asks before we can clear the contract: 1) a short attestation describing the 'surgical deletion' process for tenant data (we need steps, timeline, and audit evidence), and 2) proof that session/logs referenced by customer accounts can be deleted on demand and that copies in backups/snapshots are governed by a legal-hold path.

Attached is a trimmed SIG spreadsheet with the specific questions we couldn't reconcile. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a signed attestation and a sample artifact (redacted session log plus the deletion job run entry) within 5 business days?

Also, please include whether you support temporary retention variances for regulated customers and what compensating controls you provide.

Best,
Claire Zhou
Security Operations
Novamed Health

Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify: per-tenant delete + CAIQ/SIG evidence request

Claire —

Thanks for the SIG extract. I'm attaching our deletion flow diagram and a short write-up below — this is what we'll include in the attestation. Highlights:

- Trigger types: API delete, customer-initiated portal erase, and automated TTL job.
- Scope: tenant metadata, blobs, generated artifacts, and session logs are scoped by tenant ID and a deletion marker so KV cache and derived embeddings are included.
- Backups/snapshots: immutable backups are tagged; deletion is flagged in the metadata index and a legal-hold only toggles a 'hold' flag that prevents deletion workers from purge steps. Full removal from backups requires a forensics request and controlled restore+scrub workflow.
- Evidence: deletion job emits an audit entry (job_id, tenant_id, objects_deleted_count, timestamp, initiating_principal). We can provide a redacted job log entry and the corresponding S3 object list for one sample delete.

Operational caveats: we do not perform immediate deep-scrubbing of older snapshot copies without a separate forensics flow; that path is intended for court orders and regulatory holds and currently takes 3-10 business days depending on storage tier.

I'll prepare the artifact set (redacted session log + job audit entry + short attestation paragraph) and share via the Drive link Ben provided.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: legal@novamed.com, Marco Villa <m.villa@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-tenant delete + CAIQ/SIG evidence request

Soojin —

This is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from legal: 1) can you confirm the maximum retention window for session logs if no deletion request is made? 2) what controls prevent service engineers from restoring deleted tenant data during incident triage? We also need the redacted artifact to show the audit fields you listed.

For the retention window, Novamed's policy requires no more than 60 days of session logs unless an explicit retention variance is documented. If Redwood's default is longer we'll need the variance and compensating controls documented.

Finally, will the attestation be signed by a Security leader or Compliance? Please advise — our procurement requires a named signer.

Claire
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>
To: Claire Zhou <c.zhou@novamed.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify: per-tenant delete + CAIQ/SIG evidence request

Claire —

Thanks for the clarifying asks. Short answers and deliverables:

1) Default session-log retention: 90 days rolling by service tier. We recognize Novamed's 60-day requirement; Redwood can accommodate a tenant-scoped retention variance to 60 days. We will:
   - Apply a tenant config override that sets TTL=60d for session logs.
   - Surface the override and date-of-change in the tenant metadata index.
   - Provide a compensating control: encrypted, access-restricted backup snapshots that require two-person authorization to restore.

2) Controls to prevent engineer restores:
   - Restore workflows require a service ticket with JIRA id, an approval step from our on-call lead, and an automated audit-check that prevents restoring objects flagged with deletion_marker=true.
   - Engineers operate under scoped IAM roles; restore actions write a restore_audit record that is immutable and forwarded to the customer's audit stream when requested.

3) Artifacts: attached to Drive are (a) redacted session log sample, (b) deletion-job audit entry, and (c) a one-page attestation template signed by Redwood's Head of Security (we can circulate a signed DocuSign copy). Link: https://drive.google.com/novamed-evidence/ND-2028-1173

4) Timeline: we will provide the artifacts and DocuSign-ready attestation by Thu EOD (2028-04-19). If you confirm acceptance of the 60-day variance and the compensating controls, we'll proceed to finalize the signature.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Compliance & Risk
Redwood Inference
